title: The principal-agent problem
summary: Why the principal-agent problem arises, the owner-manager and manager-worker cases, and the incentives that solve each.

chunks.heading: What the problem is
chunks.explanation_md:
The **principal** is the one who hires; the **agent** is the one who does the work.

- **Shareholders** (principal) cannot watch the **manager** (agent) all day.
- A **manager** (principal) cannot watch every **worker** (agent).

So when profits fall, was it **low effort** or **bad luck**? The principal cannot tell. That is the **principal-agent problem**, and the fix is to **align the agent's interests** with the principal's.

key_terms.meaning: Arises when the principal cannot observe the effort of the agent

chunks.exam_line: The principal cannot tell low effort from bad luck, so incentives must align the agent with the principal.

chunks.big_idea: When the boss cannot see how hard someone works, a bad result could be laziness or bad luck, and the boss cannot tell which.

steps.label: Manager
steps.note: Agent of shareholders, principal of workers

watch_out: The manager is an **agent** to shareholders but a **principal** to workers.
chunks.exam_answer_md: The **principal-agent problem** occurs when the principal cannot observe the effort of the agent (shareholders and managers; managers and workers). The principal cannot determine whether a bad outcome was the result of the agent's low effort or bad luck, so principals must devise plans to align the agents' interests with their own.

chunks.heading: The fixes
chunks.explanation_md:
A manager who holds **stock options** gains when the share price rises, just like the shareholders. A worker on **piece rates** earns more for every unit made. That is what aligning interests means.

Outside pressure helps too: a manager who does badly risks their **reputation**, and a badly run firm can be **taken over**.
chunks.exam_line: For managers: stock options, bonuses, reputation, takeover threat. For workers: profit sharing, revenue sharing, piece rates, time clocks and spot checks.

chunks.big_idea: Pay people in ways that reward results, and add outside pressure, so their interest matches the boss's.
watch_out: Reputation and takeover are **external** incentives; stock options and bonuses are **internal**.
chunks.exam_answer_md: **Owners and managers:** internal incentives (incentive contracts, stock options, year-end bonuses) and external incentives (personal reputation, potential for takeover). **Managers and workers:** profit sharing, revenue sharing, piece rates, time clocks and spot checks.

What is the principal-agent problem? How can owners solve it with managers?
questions.model_answer_md:
The **principal-agent problem** occurs when the principal **cannot observe the agent's effort**, so a bad outcome could be low effort or bad luck. Shareholders (principal) and managers (agent) are one case.

Owners can use **internal incentives** (incentive contracts, stock options, year-end bonuses) and rely on **external incentives** (personal reputation, potential for takeover).
